dedupe_keys.name: relsad reliability tool for smart and active distribution networks

description: RELSAD (RELiability tool for Smart and Active Distribution networks) is an open Python tool for reliability assessment of modern distribution systems. It was developed by Stine Fleischer Myhre with Olav Bjarte Fosso, Poul E. Heegaard and Oddbjørn Gjerde, with releases up to 0.2.15. It runs Monte Carlo reliability analysis and sequential simulation of network behaviour with user-defined loading and failure evolution over a chosen period and time step. Active components such as microgrids, distributed generation, batteries and electric vehicles are modelled, as are ICT components such as automated switches, sensors and control systems, so that dependencies between the power and ICT systems are taken into account. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub and Zenodo under the MIT licence at no cost. Caveats: only radial systems are supported, and the last commit was in October 2022. Simulation uses are reliability and interdependency studies of distribution grids with ICT, microgrids and flexible resources. Related records: model-erad-distribution-resilience also assesses distribution resilience.
